evidence.observation: Request-scoped gateway selection. The tenant is taken from the authenticated request context (getRequestTenant()) and falls back to the user's own assigned tenant (ensureUserTenant) or the default tenant; the caller cannot inject a different tenant id here, so a request can only ever be dispatched to the tenant it is bound to. The selected tenant's WS client is fetched via ensureGatewayClient and the dispatch waits on ensureConnected.

HTTP dispatch target for the current request. Uses the same context-tenant-first selection (getRequestTenant() || ensureUserTenant(user) || getDefaultTenant()), then returns { baseUrl: http://host:port, headers: { Authorization: Bearer <tenant token> }, tenant }. This is the value the HTTP gateway layer (server/core/gateway-client.js) proxies to, so the tenant binding decides which fake/real backend receives the call.

Explicit-tenant dispatch path. Resolves the tenant id against openclaw_tenants and throws `Tenant ${tenantId} not found` before ensureGatewayClient/ensureConnected ever runs, i.e. an unresolvable tenant is rejected before any backend dispatch. This is the existence guard the demo mirrors for the mismatched/unknown tenant scenarios.

Explicit-tenant HTTP target path. Same normalizeTenant lookup + `Tenant ${tenantId} not found` throw before returning a target, so an unknown tenant never yields a baseUrl to dispatch to. Confirms that tenant resolution is a precondition of dispatch rather than a post-dispatch check.

Resolves and caches the tenant owned by the authenticated user (getTenantForUser + allocate/assign under an allocation lock). This supplies the fallback tenant that getGatewayForCurrentRequest / getHttpTargetForCurrentRequest use, and is what binds req.currentTenant in server/core/auth.js.

Maps an openclaw_tenants DB row into { id, containerName, token, host, port, maxUsers, dataSource, status }. host defaults to container_name and port defaults to 18789; host/port/token are exactly the fields composed into the dispatch baseUrl and Bearer header.

claims.claim: A request that is bound to a tenant is dispatched to that tenant's backend: getGatewayForCurrentRequest/getHttpTargetForCurrentRequest derive the tenant solely from the authenticated request context (getRequestTenant) with the user's assigned tenant as fallback, then build the WS URL / HTTP baseUrl from that tenant's host+port and token.

A mismatched or unknown tenant is rejected before dispatch: explicit tenant resolution normalizes the id out of openclaw_tenants and throws `Tenant ${tenantId} not found` before ensureGatewayClient/ensureConnected runs, so no request reaches the backend, and the request-context path cannot be redirected to a non-bound tenant at all.

Tenant routing is per-request and multi-user-safe: the tenant is bound at auth time (server/core/auth.js calls ensureTenantForUser and runs the handler inside runWithRequestContext with { user, tenant }), and every dispatch helper reads it back via getRequestTenant/getRequestUser rather than trusting a caller-supplied tenant.

conclusion: The demo shows the multi-tenant isolation contract end to end against local fake fixtures: a request bound to tenant-1 is routed to the tenant-1 fake gateway backend (HTTP 200, backend records exactly 1 dispatch carrying the tenant Bearer token), while a request that asks for tenant-2 while bound to tenant-1 is rejected with 403 before any target is built, and an unknown tenant-9 is rejected with `Tenant tenant-9 not found` before dispatch. Across all three scenarios the tenant-2 backend records 0 dispatches, proving the mismatch never leaves the routing layer.

The demo first statically re-reads server/core/multi-tenant-gateway.js and asserts that getGatewayForCurrentRequest (397-411), callGatewayForTenant (417-424), getHttpTargetForCurrentRequest (448-466) and getHttpTargetForTenantId (468-485) still contain those symbols at those line ranges, then boots two stdlib-only fake gateway backends on 127.0.0.1:19791/19792 and runs the allowed / mismatched / unknown scenarios. It is self-contained (Node >=18 global fetch, no node_modules, no Docker) because the real module imports better-sqlite3 and ws, which are not installed; the routing decision is re-implemented with the source line references kept inline. Limitation: this exercises the routing/existence-guard logic, not a live OpenClaw container.
